author: WP09
summary: Explains the four modern explicit-API renderers with a Vulkan focus: blend and stencil defect history, occlusion-query mechanics, ordered clears and usage, swapchain format and present modes, frames in flight, deferred-present readback, descriptor pools, Metal's refusals and the evidence tiers. Partly stale at 009d40f5: the 512-set ceiling, the missing SetSwapInterval override, the unresolved depth-bias failure and the coverage gap are all contradicted. The site had one-line Vulkan internals coverage of swapchain, present and snapshots, and strong Metal and capability-polarity coverage in tutorials 109 and 101; the depth was written into two Vulkan deep dives and an evidence-tiers page.

concepts.text: The modern explicit-API cluster is VULKAN, SDL_GPU, WEBGPU and METAL: they share a vocabulary (immutable pipelines, visible resource transitions, shader delivery as a build concern) but no implementation; two drive a native API directly and two go through a portable layer.

Per-identity route summary at the snapshot: VULKAN renders to RenderTarget2D and up to four MRT, has real occlusion queries and takes custom shaders only as SPIR-V words; SDL_GPU has RT2D and MRT, refuses occlusion queries by throwing and takes SPIR-V (plus Vulkan-rule GLSL where libshaderc exists); WEBGPU has RT2D, MRT, real queries and WGSL; METAL has RT2D only, refuses MRT, queries and custom effects, and compiles embedded MSL at run time.
concepts.note: The source table said VULKAN's shader boundary was CNA GLSL compiled to SPIR-V; that is the stock path, while the custom-effect intake is SPIR-V only (Vulkan_ShaderDialectContract).

concepts.text: A capability bit or a device that constructs without throwing is not feature evidence; native and browser WEBGPU are separate evidence environments even though one identity and one implementation serve both.
tokens: never promotes a no-throw smoke test

concepts.text: Recurring defect shape across these renderers: an interface accepts a complete state packet while the implementation consumes only part of it, producing plausible pictures rather than errors.

concepts.text: A recorded Vulkan validation campaign reported 4,371 passes in a 4,373-case configured population (two hardware skips) and 126 of 127 renderer-specific ctest cases, with Vulkan_DepthBias the single failure.
concepts.note: Campaign population at an older revision; the site publishes no per-renderer test count (counting rule), and at 009d40f5 the Vulkan_DepthBias failure is explained as a test defect (VULKAN-091, recorded as its own concept).

concepts.text: Before that campaign baseline the Vulkan renderer had five failing BlendState tests and three segfaulting skinned-model content tests, all closed without test exclusions.
concepts.note: Release-chronology detail of an older campaign; the blend defect itself is recorded separately as a FIXED BUG with its current mapping; the skinned crashes are not re-derivable at 009d40f5.

concepts.section: BlendState: native mapping and historical defect
concepts.text: Vulkan's blend state used to apply one hard-coded NonPremultiplied equation whenever blending was enabled, ignoring the requested Blend and BlendFunction values.
concepts.note: Fixed at 009d40f5: ApplyBlendState stores all six values (Task 868 comment) and FillBlendAttachmentState maps them in every pipeline-creation function; presented on the page as a historical case study.

concepts.section: BlendState: native mapping and historical defect
concepts.text: Current Vulkan blend mapping: ApplyBlendState stores colour and alpha source, destination and function, four per-slot ColorWriteChannels masks and the multisample mask; blending counts as enabled unless both channels are the Opaque preset; FillBlendAttachmentState applies the mapping for every pipeline; Blend.BlendFactor maps to VK_BLEND_FACTOR_CONSTANT_COLOR and the blend key is bit-packed.
Vulkan's ApplyDepthStencilState used to store only the depth-enable and depth-write flags of its sixteen parameters, so no pipeline ever enabled the stencil test.
concepts.note: Fixed at 009d40f5: ApplyDepthStencilState stores every value and FillDepthStencilState bakes them into every 3D pipeline (Task 870); historical case study on the page.

concepts.text: Current Vulkan depth-stencil mapping: FillDepthStencilState writes depthCompareOp, stencilTestEnable and front and back VkStencilOpState into every 3D pipeline; with TwoSidedStencilMode false the back face copies the front (FNA behaviour); compare mask, write mask and reference are dynamic per-draw state.

The first stencil repair swapped the counter-clockwise operations onto the front face on a software-driver hypothesis; VKPAR-0005 measured on an AMD RADV device that this inverted all three operations. Clockwise-as-displayed is the front face and the counter-clockwise fields go to the back face.
concepts.note: Not in the source unit; TARGET extends the stencil story and corrects its implied final state.

concepts.text: GraphicsDevice.ReferenceStencil is an independent device property; Vulkan overrides SetReferenceStencil to change it without re-applying DepthStencilState. The source unit's statement that EasyGL remained the exception is stale: EasyGL overrides SetReferenceStencil as well.
tokens: EasyGL renderer overrides it as well

concepts.text: The device-wide Vulkan depth format once tried the stencil-less D32_SFLOAT first; FindDepthFormat now tries D24_UNORM_S8_UINT, D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT, then D32_SFLOAT and throws if none supports depth-stencil attachment, and StencilBuffer is answered from the format actually chosen.

concepts.section: OcclusionQuery: current contract and render-pass limit
concepts.text: Vulkan occlusion queries are tags: Begin() marks the query active without recording a command, PushPending3DDraw tags 3D draws, RecordCommandBuffer resets every tagged query with vkCmdResetQueryPool before any render pass and wraps each contiguous run of tagged draws in one vkCmdBeginQuery/vkCmdEndQuery pair.

concepts.section: OcclusionQuery: current contract and render-pass limit
concepts.text: Limitation: only the first contiguous run of a query's draws per frame is recorded (a recorded query is never reopened without a reset), so a query spanning a render-pass boundary does not sum the draws after it; the open query closes at each pass end.
tokens: Only the first contiguous run per frame is counted

target.evidence: modules/renderers/vulkan/src/VulkanRenderer.cpp (draw3DFor 'reject additional spans beyond the first contiguous run'; closeOpenQuery3D at pass end)

concepts.section: OcclusionQuery: current contract and render-pass limit
concepts.text: Exact occlusion counts need the occlusionQueryPrecise feature and VK_QUERY_CONTROL_PRECISE_BIT (VULKAN-370), reported by OcclusionQuery::isPixelCountPreciseEXT; an empty span completes immediately with zero (VKPAR-0026); a disposed query is detached from queued draws and its pool retired behind the frame fence (REMED-GFX-075).

concepts.section: OcclusionQuery: current contract and render-pass limit
concepts.text: Vulkan occlusion evidence: Vulkan_OcclusionQuery_PixelCount checks a visible quad, an occluded quad and two non-overlapping half-quads summed in one span; Vulkan_OcclusionQuery_Precision asserts an exact fragment count; Vulkan_OcclusionQuery_Cycle covers reset and reuse.
concepts.note: The source unit said the checks discriminated on the project's own software Vulkan implementation; the page does not repeat an execution claim (not executed here).

concepts.section: OcclusionQuery: current contract and render-pass limit
concepts.text: Only 3D draws carry the Vulkan occlusion-query tag, so SpriteBatch batches drawn between Begin() and End() do not contribute to the count on this renderer (reading of the source, not executed).
concepts.note: Extension found at TARGET; recorded as an issue candidate.

target.evidence: modules/renderers/vulkan/src/VulkanRenderer.cpp (PushPending3DDraw is the only tagging site; drawSpritesFor records no query)

concepts.text: OcclusionQuery's public surface is Begin(), End(), getIsCompleteProperty() and getPixelCountProperty(); the visibility-culling pattern draws a cheap proxy inside Begin/End and consumes the result one or more frames later without blocking.
On Vulkan, keep render-target changes outside an OcclusionQuery's Begin()/End() span, because draws after a render-pass boundary are not summed.
tokens: Keep render-target changes outside a query

concepts.text: The 'unresolved' extreme DepthBias observation was a test defect: Vulkan_DepthBias used OpenGL's depth convention (z = 0 as mid-range) whereas XNA and Vulkan put z = 0 on the near plane; VULKAN-091 corrected the test after an off-screen experiment showed vkCmdSetDepthBias correct on lavapipe and RADV, and added a guard leg at z = 0.
A Vulkan render target that was cleared and unbound without any draw never entered command recording, because passes were discovered only from draws, and stayed black.
concepts.note: Fixed: Task 875, later superseded by the PendingClear ordered-clear stream (REMED-GFX-129); regression Vulkan_RenderTarget2D_ClearOnlyRoundtrip registered.

concepts.text: Each public Clear on Vulkan is a PendingClear record carrying a shared destination reference, bind-cycle segment, public command-stream order, requested aspects and values; command recording discovers clear-only segments from that stream.

SpriteBatch content rendered into all six RenderTargetCube faces and sampled through EnvironmentMapEffect after unbinding came out black; the regression now expects the blue centre, and the fixing commit was never identified.
concepts.note: Closed per CNA's records; not executed here; fixing commit unknown (a cube-view rewrite is only a plausible cause).

concepts.text: CNA's own docs/rendertarget-support.md still lists these Vulkan render-target defects and features (mips, MSAA, custom viewport) as open at the snapshot; source and registered regressions are the better evidence.

REMED-GFX-129: on Vulkan a clear that precedes every draw of its cycle rides the pass load action only on a discarding target; every other clear, and every clear on a preserving target, is recorded as vkCmdClearAttachments after the preceding slice of draws; ClearDepth and ClearStencil record ordered clears of just their aspects.

Vulkan clear details: the clear rectangle is always the whole render area (viewport and scissor never restrict Clear, REMED-GFX-018); a stencil request on a depth-only format drops the stencil bit; the first back-buffer cycle of a frame always clears because an acquired swapchain image is undefined.

Clear evidence: Vulkan_GraphicsDevice_ClearOptions encodes surviving colour, depth and stencil aspects into colour probes; the shared ordered-clear fixture queues each whole sequence before any readback so a renderer cannot pass by being forced to settle between commands.
concepts.note: The source unit called the ClearOptions fixture 'eight-mask'; not re-verified, so the page does not repeat that figure.

concepts.text: Render-target usage follows one shared predicate, RenderTargetUsagePreservesContentsEXT: only DiscardContents discards, PreserveContents and PlatformContents both preserve, as in FNA.
On a DiscardContents bind GraphicsDevice clears colour to opaque black and, where the attachments really exist, depth to 1 and stencil to 0; an explicit ordered clear supersedes either usage policy.

Vulkan render-pass variants follow usage: single-sample and MSAA caches provide clear and load variants; preserving depth-stencil attachments keep layouts and store ops across unbind and rebind; cube colour is per face while one depth-stencil image is shared by all six faces, matching FNA.

Optional Vulkan device features are negotiated: fillModeNonSolid and samplerAnisotropy (and at the snapshot also independentBlend, occlusionQueryPrecise, drawIndirectFirstInstance, textureCompressionBC and the 4444 format extension) are enabled only when reported, and the capability answers follow; a missing feature is not a creation failure.
concepts.note: The source unit's note that this investigation found no bug is kept on the page as a negative finding.

concepts.text: VulkanRenderer::SupportsCapability has no default arm and the family compiles with -Werror=switch, so a new GraphicsCapability member stops the build until Vulkan answers it, and an out-of-range value is refused.

Vulkan RenderTargetCube MSAA uses a separate multisampled 2D image with six array layers and one view per face (REMED-GFX-141), resolved into the single-sample cube-compatible colour image; transient only for a discarding target, so a preserving face can be reloaded.

At most four render targets can be bound; the cap is CNA's shared MAX_RENDERTARGET_BINDINGS in GraphicsDevice mirroring FNA, not a Vulkan device limit; the MultipleRenderTargets capability answers maxColorAttachments > 1 and the public answer is also limited by the profile.
Plain Texture2D uploads above level 0 go through UpdatePixelsLevel into the requested subresource on Vulkan (Vulkan_Texture2D_Mip_RoundTrip); upper levels are authored by the game.

The source unit said non-Color formats remain blocked on Vulkan by the shared Texture::ValidateFormat rule; at the snapshot Vulkan classifies every format it can store against the device's VkFormatProperties (VULKAN-170) and defers only unmapped formats.
concepts.note: The Color-only framework rule applies only to formats Vulkan has no mapping for; docs/rendering-backends.html#texture-formats already states the per-renderer table.

concepts.text: Vulkan render-target mip generation: VulkanTargetPassEXT::MaybeGenerateMips runs a per-level vkCmdBlitImage cascade with linear filtering from resolved level 0 after the pass; RenderTarget2D and RenderTargetCube both resolve MSAA.

Each SpriteBatch batch and 3D draw on Vulkan snapshots the active viewport (REMED-GFX-062), scissor (REMED-GFX-013) and blend factor at enqueue and applies them while replaying, so later state cannot retroactively change earlier queued draws.

Vulkan scissor replay clamps an enabled rectangle to the target and expands a disabled or zero-area rectangle to the full target before vkCmdSetScissor; the viewport is deliberately not clamped (it is a transform) and its depth range is clamped to [0, 1].
CNA's docs/rendertarget-support.md lists render-target mips, MSAA and custom viewport as open for Vulkan although source and tests implement them.
concepts.note: Staleness of a CNA-internal Markdown file (still stale at 009d40f5); the site records the current behaviour on the Vulkan state page and mentions the stale document once (see the clear-history concept).

concepts.section: How a swapchain gets built: format, color space, and present mode
concepts.text: VulkanRenderer::CreateSwapchain decides once, at swapchain creation, the presented pixel format and the VkPresentModeKHR, instead of accepting whatever the driver lists first.

concepts.section: UNORM, not SRGB: a deliberate color-space decision
concepts.text: Vulkan prefers the B8G8R8A8_UNORM / SRGB_NONLINEAR surface pair because XNA's SurfaceFormat::Color is a linear byte format (ColorSrgbEXT is the encoded variant); an sRGB swapchain would lighten every frame; the search falls back to the first listed pair.

concepts.section: UNORM, not SRGB: a deliberate color-space decision
concepts.text: colorSpace describes the display's expected colour space while format decides whether stores are encoded, so UNORM with SRGB_NONLINEAR is not a contradiction; changing the one line to an sRGB format would alter the brightness of every scene.

concepts.section: UNORM, not SRGB: a deliberate color-space decision
concepts.text: The Vulkan constructor ignores the requested backBufferFormat, depthStencilFormat and isFullScreen create arguments; VULKAN-348 reports the formats really in effect (always Color, the real depth format) and GraphicsDevice writes them back into PresentationParameters.
concepts.note: The source unit said the factory discards the formats; at TARGET it still ignores them but reports the applied values back.

concepts.section: UNORM, not SRGB: a deliberate color-space decision
concepts.text: The Vulkan back buffer always owns a depth-stencil image (D24S8, then D32S8, then D32) even for DepthFormat::None; render targets choose their depth format per instance and None means no attachment there; fullscreen and resize follow the surface through swapchain rebuilds.

concepts.section: SwapInterval to VkPresentModeKHR: the same three-way switch Chapter ch:game-loop introduced
concepts.text: PresentInterval maps to VkPresentModeKHR on Vulkan: 0 prefers IMMEDIATE then MAILBOX then FIFO; 1 uses FIFO; 2 prefers FIFO_RELAXED then FIFO.

concepts.section: SwapInterval to VkPresentModeKHR: the same three-way switch Chapter ch:game-loop introduced
concepts.text: FIFO is the only present mode Vulkan guarantees, which is why every fallback chain ends in it; PresentInterval::Two maps to FIFO_RELAXED, which tolerates a late frame rather than halving the refresh rate as the Direct3D 9 reading suggests.
tokens: Why Two is not half the refresh rate
concepts.note: FIFO_RELAXED timing is the Vulkan specification's contract; no CNA test times it.

concepts.section: SwapInterval to VkPresentModeKHR: the same three-way switch Chapter ch:game-loop introduced
concepts.text: The source unit stated that Vulkan does not override SetSwapInterval, that GraphicsDevice::Reset therefore cannot change the present mode, and that no test queries the real present mode.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 SetSwapInterval rebuilds the swapchain (VULKAN-332), Reset forwards the interval, and Vulkan_SwapInterval asserts the live present mode; the historical state is described on the Vulkan presentation page.

concepts.section: SwapInterval to VkPresentModeKHR: the same three-way switch Chapter ch:game-loop introduced
concepts.text: VULKAN-332: SetSwapInterval records the request, ignores an unchanged interval and otherwise rebuilds the swapchain through RecreateSwapchain; GraphicsDevice::Reset forwards PresentationInterval to every renderer; GetAppliedPresentModeEXT and SupportsUnsynchronisedPresentModeEXT expose what the device gave; Vulkan_SwapInterval uses the live mode, not the recorded interval, as its oracle.

concepts.section: SwapInterval to VkPresentModeKHR: the same three-way switch Chapter ch:game-loop introduced
concepts.text: Because CNA's Game owns its GraphicsDevice before a derived constructor runs, SynchronizeWithVerticalRetrace only reaches the renderer through ApplyChanges and Reset; before the repairs an ordinary Vulkan game that disabled vsync stayed in FIFO.

concepts.section: Two frames in flight, and the deferred-present trick that makes readback pixel-safe
concepts.text: Vulkan double-buffers CPU work against the GPU: MaxFramesInFlight is a constexpr 2, with one fence, an image-available and a render-finished semaphore and one command buffer per slot, indexed by a wrapping currentFrame_; sync objects are indexed by slot, not swapchain image.

Ordinary present sequence: wait the slot fence, process retired resources, acquire (OUT_OF_DATE recreates and returns before the fence reset), reset fence and command buffer, record, submit waiting on image-available at colour output, present waiting on render-finished, advance the slot.

The three Vulkan primitives answer three questions: the fence whether the CPU may reuse the slot, the image-available semaphore whether the GPU may write the acquired image, the render-finished semaphore whether the presentation engine may display it.
tokens: Each primitive answers exactly one question

concepts.section: The deferred path: why GetBackBufferData cannot simply call Present
concepts.text: GetBackBufferData on Vulkan uses SubmitFrame(true): the swapchain image is copied into a staging buffer inside the frame's command buffer, the present is held until the CPU has read it, and FinishDeferredPresent presents exactly once afterwards, so readback never races the compositor or drops a frame.

Vulkan's readback cache re-renders only when draws are pending, the cache was invalidated (every Clear variant; swapchain recreation, VULKAN-404) or the staging buffer no longer covers the extent; re-presenting an empty queue would otherwise destroy the content later reads of the same frame should return.

When the first-frame acquire is out of date (noted as common under Wayland with RADV) ReadBackbuffer zero-fills the output and returns so a caller can detect a blank frame and retry, rather than throwing or returning stale data.
tokens: A blank first frame is reported, not thrown

concepts.text: ReadBackbuffer swaps blue and red only when the swapchain format is a B8G8R8A8 format and writes zero for requested pixels outside the extent.
tokens: Byte order is checked, not assumed

concepts.text: The source unit described a hard ceiling of 512 simultaneously live Texture2D plus RenderTarget2D objects on Vulkan, with the 513th throwing at construction.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 (and already at the source unit's pin) 512 is the capacity of each combined-image-sampler pool; pools chain (VULKAN-390/181/391) and a named exception is thrown only if the device refuses another pool.

concepts.text: Vulkan descriptor pools grow: AllocateTexSamplerDescSetEXT tries the newest overflow pool, then the base pool, then chains another 512-set pool; Texture2D and RenderTarget2D allocate through it; a named runtime_error is thrown only when the device refuses a new pool; sets return to their owning pool through fenced retirement; GetTexSamplerDescriptorPoolCountEXT exposes the pool count.

Stock-effect descriptor pools are created with kEffectPoolMaxSets (512 * MaxFramesInFlight) sets and, with the custom-effect path, chain further pools through AllocateFromGrowingPoolEXT; a caller that still gets no set refuses by name rather than binding a null set.

When the single sampler-descriptor pool was full, Vulkan returned its default white descriptor set, drawing white sprites silently; after chaining was added, Texture2D and RenderTarget2D still bypassed the growing pool until a RADV run of Vulkan_DescriptorCapacityContract failed every leg.
concepts.note: Fixed at 009d40f5: all allocations go through the chaining helper; the case study is on the Vulkan state page.

target.evidence: modules/renderers/vulkan/src/VulkanRenderer.cpp (GetOrCreateTexSamplerDescSet VULKAN-390 comment; VulkanTextureRenderer constructor VULKAN-181/391 comment)

concepts.text: Vulkan_DescriptorPoolOverflow injects VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_POOL_MEMORY because exhaustion is unreachable by volume on the tested drivers; it checks single-pool chaining, 640 index-coloured live textures, the named exception and a silent validation layer.
Per-effect descriptor pools on Vulkan are separate from the texture pool, so the texture-pool behaviour does not govern how many objects can use a given stock effect.

The source unit reported no Vulkan pixel tests for SpriteBatch sort, rotation, scale, crop and flip, SpriteFont glyph placement or multi-mesh Model hierarchies; at the snapshot such registrations exist, reusing the shared EasyGL sources.
concepts.note: Registration only; not executed here.

concepts.text: Missing renderer-specific tests do not mean the shared C++ code is wrong; they mean the feature has not been independently re-verified on that renderer's path.

concepts.section: METAL: a narrow implementation with explicit refusals
concepts.text: METAL is macOS-only, compiles Objective-C++, links Apple frameworks and passes an embedded MSL string to newLibraryWithSource: at run time, which simplifies packaging but makes shader compilation part of start-up.

concepts.section: METAL: a narrow implementation with explicit refusals
concepts.text: METAL implements extended primitive submission and RenderTarget2D but refuses MRT, MSAA (reported as zero), custom effects, occlusion queries, instancing, multi-stream input and back-buffer readback, each refusal citing missing macOS evidence.

concepts.section: METAL: a narrow implementation with explicit refusals
concepts.text: METAL's automated macOS lane proves construction, clear/present and capability reporting (Metal_Smoke, Metal_Capabilities, Metal_PortableHelpers under Metal validation) but no representative 3D pixels.
The renderer contract's default-true capability polarity makes accidental overclaiming easy, so a false answer is authored while a true answer may be an unrevisited default.

Explicit refusal as an integration pattern: enumerate the unsupported surface, throw at the boundary with a reason, and widen it only when a platform-specific observation proves the new path; SDL_GPU's occlusion refusal, Vulkan's named descriptor exceptions and WebGPU's float-target refusals follow it.
tokens: Explicit refusal as an integration pattern

concepts.text: VULKAN has the broadest renderer-specific pixel history of the four, under a Khronos validation output gate, yet no workflow gates the full suite, it is outside the 32-fixture parity corpus and has no real-XNA comparison.
SDL_GPU is exercised through the native driver SDL selects (Vulkan on Linux); that is not proof of every driver; Direct3D 12 evidence is a Wine and vkd3d-proton probe and no Metal run is recorded.
tokens: One identity sits over several native APIs

concepts.text: WEBGPU has native (Linux x86_64) and browser (headless Chrome, by script) evidence, which remain separate qualifications; no workflow selects it.

Record both axes for any result: which CNA identity ran and which native driver or device path served it; one abstraction selecting Vulkan on one machine and Metal on another does not turn one run into proof of both.
tokens: Record the identity and the native driver

issues.text: Vulkan occlusion queries record only the first contiguous run of tagged draws per frame; draws after a render-pass boundary inside one Begin/End span are not summed.
On VULKAN only 3D draws are tagged with the active OcclusionQuery; SpriteBatch draws between Begin and End do not contribute to PixelCount.
An enabled zero-area ScissorRectangle draws unclipped on VULKAN and SDL_GPU (expanded to the full target) but clips everything on WEBGPU and suppresses the draw on METAL.
CNA's docs/rendertarget-support.md still lists implemented Vulkan render-target features (mips, MSAA, viewport, black-frame defects) as open (documentation staleness inside CNA).
No test times the real cadence of Vulkan present modes; FIFO_RELAXED late-frame behaviour is the specification's contract only.
Vulkan applied one hard-coded NonPremultiplied blend equation whenever blending was on (Task 868).
Vulkan ApplyDepthStencilState discarded every stencil parameter and never enabled the stencil test (Task 870).
Vulkan device-wide depth format preferred the stencil-less D32_SFLOAT, so stencil almost never worked.
Vulkan occlusion queries were disconnected from deferred draw submission and always reported zero.
Extreme RasterizerState.DepthBias produced no visible bias on Vulkan (recorded as an unresolved observation).
A Vulkan render target cleared and unbound without a draw stayed black (never recorded).
A Vulkan RenderTargetCube filled by SpriteBatch and sampled through EnvironmentMapEffect after unbinding rendered black.
Vulkan did not override SetSwapInterval, so SynchronizeWithVerticalRetrace plus ApplyChanges could not change the present mode.
Vulkan limited simultaneously live Texture2D plus RenderTarget2D objects to 512 (one fixed descriptor pool).
No Vulkan-specific pixel tests for SpriteBatch sort/rotation/scale/crop/flip, SpriteFont placement or multi-mesh Model hierarchies.
METAL refuses MRT, MSAA, custom effects, occlusion queries, instancing, multi-stream input and back-buffer readback.
METAL's CI lane proves construction, clear/present and capability reporting but no representative 3D pixels.
